name: John
bio: John, son of Zebedee, was mending fishing nets with his father and brother James when Jesus called the two brothers to follow him; they immediately left the boat and their father to do so (Matthew 4:21-22). His place among Jesus's closest disciples, and his later authorship of a Gospel, three letters, and Revelation, are told in detail in the chapters and books ahead. He is a different figure from John the Baptist. He, along with Peter and his brother James, was taken by Jesus up a mountain to witness his transfiguration with Moses and Elijah (Matthew 17:1-8). On the way to Jerusalem, his mother asked Jesus that he and his brother James sit at Jesus's right and left in his kingdom; Jesus told them they would share his suffering, though such honors were the Father's to grant (Matthew 20:20-23). He, along with Peter and his brother James, was taken by Jesus deeper into Gethsemane to pray, though he fell asleep each time Jesus checked on them (Matthew 26:36-45). When Jesus named the twelve apostles, he surnamed John and his brother James "Boanerges," meaning "sons of thunder" (Mark 3:17). When a Samaritan village refused to receive Jesus as he set out for Jerusalem, John and his brother James asked if he wanted them to call down fire on it as Elijah had done; Jesus rebuked them for the suggestion (Luke 9:51-56). Jesus sent John and Peter specifically to prepare the Passover meal for the Last Supper (Luke 22:8). At the Last Supper, "the disciple whom Jesus loved" reclined next to him and, prompted by Peter, asked who would betray him; this disciple, never named in John's Gospel, is traditionally identified as John himself, consistent with the Gospel's own closing claim that its author was the disciple Jesus loved (John 13:23-25; 21:20-24). At Jesus's arrest, another disciple, known to the high priest, accompanied Peter into the high priest's courtyard and arranged for him to be let in; John does not name this disciple, though some identify him with the author himself (John 18:15-16). As Jesus hung on the cross, he entrusted his mother to the care of "the disciple whom he loved," traditionally identified as John; that disciple took her into his own home from that hour (John 19:26-27). When Mary Magdalene reported the empty tomb, the disciple Jesus loved ran there with Peter and outran him, though he let Peter enter first; seeing the grave clothes left behind, he believed (John 20:2-8).
